clue.text: Crazy to return and question the material

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way one came, so the word for crazy is read from right to left

parts.note: crazy means mad
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone tells a mad person to come back and interrogate the cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' is the reversal signal; 'Crazy' looks like a comment on the material but is a synonym to be turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a woven fabric with a reversible figured pattern, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Down-and-out cried, getting let off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tramp weeps on being released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles CRIED and LET together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict is a destitute vagrant, someone with no home or means.

clue.text: Not a word which ever way you look at it

indicators.text: which ever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading from either end gives the same letters, so the answer reads the same both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent no matter how a matter is viewed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: the same letters forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum means saying nothing at all, staying silent.

clue.text: Ale so tiny it's of no significance?

definitions.meaning: weak, thin beer of low strength

explanation.definitionFit: Small beer was weak ale, and the phrase came to mean trivial matters of little consequence.

clue.text: Survival rations? In a nut-shell, I'm taking a thousand back

indicators.note: In, paired with shell, says one thing sits within another's casing
a nut-shell wraps round its kernel, so the nut's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: a pecan is a nut

indicators.note: back means the letters of the following words run in reverse order

parts.note: I'm gives its letters without the apostrophe
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone explains survival food briefly while claiming to be taking a large sum back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the I'm and thousand pieces, and 'In a nut-shell' wraps the nut round them. The phrase pretends to mean 'briefly', its everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pemmican is dried meat pounded with fat, a compact high-energy food carried by explorers.

clue.text: Slip one casually into the fifth letter

indicators.note: done casually, without care, so the letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone slips an extra one into a letter without much care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' rearranges SLIP ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Sum up one hundred melodies

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
the Roman numeral for a hundred is C

explanation.surface: Someone totals up a hundred tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the reversal signal in this down light: 'Sum up' poses as the phrase meaning summarise.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodies are tunes, and tunes collectively are music.

clue.text: Acid cuts, so a different soap ingredient is needed

indicators.note: made different means the letters are put into another order

explanation.surface: Acid has been cut, so the soap needs another component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges ACID CUTS SO A. Caustic soda is an alkali, not an acid, which the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium hydroxide, known as caustic soda, reacts with fats to make soap.

clue.text: Deny a duck could be despatched by drowning

indicators.note: could be signals the letters may become something else when rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Someone denies that a duck might be killed by drowning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges DENYA with O. A duck is a nil score in cricket, shaped like the figure 0.
explanation.definitionFit: A noyade was an execution carried out by drowning, notoriously during the French Revolution.

clue.text: Declare rising politician has face-lift

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, last letter first

parts.note: to aver is to declare
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An announcement that an up-and-coming politician has had cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' is the reversal signal in this down light; 'rising politician' pretends to be one up-and-coming MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A revamp is a renovation that gives something a fresh look, like a makeover.

clue.text: Confusing gears on an incline, they run wildly out of control

definitions.text: they run wildly out of control

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the first piece comes before it

parts.note: a ramp is an incline

indicators.note: confusing the letters muddles them into another order

explanation.surface: Someone struggles with bicycle gears on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusing' is the anagram signal and 'on' places the incline first, as one piece put after another in an across light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampagers are people who go on a rampage, charging about violently.

clue.text: Impertinent to assert copper has retreated inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to assert is to say

indicators.note: retreated means gone backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: It is cheeky to claim that a policeman has gone back indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has retreated' reverses the copper symbol and 'inside' places it within the verb. 'Copper' looks like a policeman going back indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Impertinent and cheeky behaviour is saucy, boldly disrespectful.

clue.text: Beat the Spanish and the French, gaining the plate

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
el is Spanish for 'the'
la is French (feminine) for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes the Spanish and the French to win the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a sporting win for a plate trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamella is a thin layer or plate, as in the gills of a mushroom.

clue.text: Academic gear for the bricklayer

definitions.meaning: the flat square cap worn with a graduate's gown
the square board on which a bricklayer carries mortar

explanation.definitionFit: A mortarboard is a square academic cap, and also a bricklayer's hawk for carrying mortar.

clue.text: Cold tea needs stirring, it's found

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: The tea has gone cold and must be stirred, someone discovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs stirring' rearranges COLD TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found has been discovered or situated, its position pinned down.

clue.text: In riot, corner cops need written communication

indicators.note: in riot means in disorder, so the letters run wild

explanation.surface: During a riot, police on the corner need letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In riot' rearranges CORNER COPS NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters exchanged between people make up their correspondence.

clue.text: Masterminds, these professionals?

definitions.meaning: a verb: plans and directs a scheme
qualified people who design and build machines and structures

explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a plan is to contrive it; engineers are also trained technical experts.

clue.text: In his estimation, it's fool's gold old bob held

definitions.text: In his estimation, it's fool's gold old bob held

indicators.note: held means one piece is gripped inside the others

parts.note: an ass is a fool; the setter takes the plural, asses
or is gold in heraldry
a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: An expert valuer declares a nugget is pyrite, the old coin clutched in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' signals the shilling sitting inside. 'fool's' has to give the plural form of the beast, which the apostrophe does not strictly support. The whole clue pictures a valuer pronouncing on worthless ore.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is an official who estimates value, the person whose estimation decides.

clue.text: Racing o'er spire confuses them?

indicators.note: confuses means the letters are jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: Birds flying fast over a church steeple might lose their bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confuses' rearranges RACING O'ER SPIRE, which gives PIGEONS: the grid's PIGIONS is a misspelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Homing birds used to carry messages are raced over long distances, steeples and all.

clue.text: Increase general mayhem

indicators.note: mayhem is chaos, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Widespread chaos grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mayhem' rearranges GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge something is to make it bigger, to expand it.

clue.text: Crime against the virtuous is indecent

indicators.note: against means up against, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: pi is short for pious, virtuous
racy means risqué, slightly indecent

explanation.surface: A complaint that an offence against good people is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, crossword shorthand for pious, sits against RACY.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea, or copying protected work without permission, both offences.

clue.text: Outcome of disorder the queen dismissed as sleazy

indicators.note: the outcome of a shake-up is the letters rearranged
dismissed means the queen's letters are sent away from the pool

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The result of a disturbance, which the monarch waved off as squalid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' takes ER from DISORDER, leaving DISORD, and 'Outcome of' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid means morally squalid and seedy, much like sleazy.

clue.text: Revolutionary piece in exam

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A rebel's work appears in a test paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Revolutionary' means going round in a circle, like a satellite, not rebellious.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbital describes motion revolving around a body, like a satellite circling Earth.

clue.text: Crude cut in garment

indicators.note: crude means roughly made, so the letters are put roughly into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough slash in some clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' rearranges CUT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose, usually belted, piece of clothing.

clue.text: Manage the valley's land-tenure system

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it
a dale is a valley; the 's is surface only

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of how farmland in the valley is held.
explanation.walkthrough: Rundale was a system, in Ireland and Scotland, of holding land in scattered strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Rundale divided farmland into scattered strips held jointly by tenants, a way of holding land.

clue.text: It was a tie that caused this strained expression?

definitions.text: It was a tie that caused this strained expression?

parts.words: It was a tie that caused this strained expression?
parts.note: a game ending level and a face pinched by strain share one word

explanation.definitionFit: A match that ends level is described this way, as is a face looking tired and tense.

clue.text: Garden features boulders flanking the lake

indicators.note: flanking means lying on both sides of the other piece

parts.note: boulders are rocks
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Gardens have big stones beside a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanking' means the boulders go on both sides of the lake, the final S landing after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockeries are garden beds built of stones and planted with alpines.

clue.text: Converse well

parts.note: the opposite of healthy; converse reads as chat but means the reverse

explanation.definitionFit: Being sick is the opposite of being in good health.

clue.text: Action channel disrupted — taken off

indicators.note: disrupted means broken apart, so the first word is split by the second

parts.note: a deed is an action
a duct is a channel

explanation.surface: A broadcast channel is interrupted and removed from air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' looks like an anagram signal, but here it means the action is split open to take the channel.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount deducted has been subtracted from a total.

clue.text: Tree god featured in stone

parts.note: the ash is a tree
a lar was a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A tree spirit is carved in rock.
explanation.walkthrough: LAR is one of the Lares, household gods of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is finely dressed building stone cut into square blocks.
